farmingoverhaul:FarmGuide-text: Welcome to the Farming Guide! Here you will find everything there is to know about the changes to the Farming system. All crops have had their growth speed extended and yields tweaked to better reflect real life. Keeping it simple, grains drop less, vegetables drop more. You should let vegetables flower to harvest their seeds! One flowering crop is enough for 10-20 new crops. Grains and legumes (and pineapple and pumkin) give seeds in the crafting grid. Crop Growth Speed no longer tied to Nutrients or Moisture: Your crops will have the same growth speed no matter the soil. Crop specific watering needs: Grains could not care less about being watered, let the rain do the work (Flax too). Vegetables are a different story, but as a good rule of thumb you should try to keep the soil moisture between 80% to 60%. It is ok to go outside that range for a day or two, just don't stay there. Rain raises moisture to 75% and water next to farmland raises it to 100% so planting RIGHT next to water is not viable (unless you grow rice, in which case it is strictly advised). Nutrients affect yield: Not all crops are affected the same by this. Cereals are not really affected by poor soils, fast-growing leafy vegetables are greatly influenced and everything else is in between. A few tips: Your grains will not be eaten by animals so no need to fence them in. Use your compost! Terra preta is cool, but better fertilize your turnips first. Dirt won't feed you through the winter! “Farming is a profession of hope.” ~ Brian Brett
